message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the most recent common ancestor of the two families **Felidae** (cats) and **Equidae** (horses).  
In phylogenetic terms, that ancestor lies at the base of the clade that contains the orders **Carnivora** (which includes cats) and **Perissodactyla** (which includes horses). In other words, it is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals that gave rise to both the carnivore lineage leading to lions and the odd‑toed ungulate lineage leading to zebras.
